answer: Island-Seeded Work Ledger: each new identity must complete a small task whose output is checked only against a random sample of prior identities from a disjoint cohort. Forgery costs scale with cohort overlap: a sybil cluster's own members dominate its sample, so a false claim survives only if the attacker also forges at least half the cohort, pushing marginal cost to the nadir of cheap batch creation. Every extra identity raises the required verified-work fraction, letting attackers forge only at rising per-identity expense.
